title: The 13,000-Foot Alien Antenna Found on the Ocean Floor

segments.narration: Cameras captured a geometric tower thirteen thousand feet underwater. In 1964, an Antarctic research ship snapped a photo of something impossible in the pitch-black abyss. A slender pole stood in the mud with perfect, symmetrical crossbars.
It looked like a modern broadcast antenna sitting where no human could walk. UFO researchers seized on the photo, insisting it was an alien relay probe or a secret military device.
segments.visual_query: deep sea underwater ocean abyss mud

segments.narration: Could a natural organism really form such flawless, mechanical right angles? Conspiracy theorists argued it was impossible, especially when naval experts confirmed no military tech was ever dropped there.
But the mystery vanished when marine biologists matched the photograph to drawings from an 1888 deep-sea study. The object wasn't metal or machinery at all—it was living tissue.
It was Cladorhiza concrescens, a bizarre carnivorous ocean sponge that grows symmetrical branches to snag prey in pitch-black currents. Nature had simply designed its own underwater antenna.

accuracy_flags.claim: Oceanographers examined physical seabed samples dredged from the area to identify the object.
accuracy_flags.note: The object was identified by matching the 1964 photograph to existing drawings published in an 1888 book by Alexander Agassiz, not by examining physical seabed samples dredged from the location.
